questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided because other drivers will see you.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. It is important to know what is behind you. Make mirror checks part of your normal driving routine.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection on its own.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, a jacket should be worn:

options.text: No matter what the weather is.
Only if the ride will be longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what the weather is.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration in hot weather.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you are fit to ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a limit beforehand so you can still safely ride.
Not worry about your riding abilities if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Alcohol can impair your abilities. The safest choice is to not ride.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals can be used instead of or along with turn signals. When the left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgating is to let the other driver pass. If it is safe, change lanes and allow them ahead of you. Speeding up will only make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle. Inspect your tires, oil and fluid levels, lights, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should your clothing do?

options.text: Be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Not cover your arms or legs completely.
Not include a jacket if the weather is warm.

questions.explanation: Good clothing can protect you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothes should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What type of sign is usually rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. These signs tell you the road rules you must follow.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left side of your lane.
Don't worry about where you position yourself.
Always ride on the far right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. This position makes it most likely the driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal covers are all slippery surfaces. Ride with extra care on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection usually take, and when should you do it?

options.text: A few minutes, no more than once a month.
A few minutes, before every ride.
Over an hour, and done by a mechanic.
Over an hour, only if you're carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes, before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a full pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: What lane position should riders generally use?

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose the position that gives you the most space and safety.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose the position that gives you the most space and safety.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position changes too. Pick the position that gives you the most space around you and helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Stop your wheels from skidding and locking up.
Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop your wheels from skidding and locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS stops your wheels from skidding and locking up when you brake hard in emergencies. It works by having sensors detect when a wheel might lock. When this happens, the system releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep your brakes working at their best.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should riders watch out for?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking space.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. A car may pull away from the curb or back out of a parking space without warning.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle fit you properly?

options.text: When you can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
When you can reach the controls by stretching.
When the handlebars go over your head.
When your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you if your feet can reach the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to easily reach and use all the controls.

questions.question: What is the single best thing you can do to survive a motorcycle accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce your chance of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other food and drinks. This means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, it enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. The body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, you should ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It gives you a better view of the road ahead.
It limits your view of the road ahead.
It makes it hard to see past the vehicle.
It lets the other driver go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see further ahead and makes you more visible to other drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: To avoid serious injury in a crash, you should do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: You can reduce injury risk by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing. A windshield is not a required safety measure.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no visible damage. Appearance does not affect safety.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are rare on roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look far ahead to spot possible hazards. This helps you react to dangers before you reach them.

questions.question: To stay in control of your motorcycle while turning, you should:

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright without leaning.
Look through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look through the turn by turning your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: An outer shell that resists impact.
An inner liner that absorbs impact.

questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers can keep you awake but cannot lower your blood alcohol or make you sober.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
